**Author:** Alex Volkov (@altryne — AI newsletter author, prolific tools commenter) · posted 2026-09-18 00:09Z · received 2026-09-19T17:15:39Z (WhatsApp via RDP-30, routed by CoS). Stats at capture: 150 replies; likes/views not exposed by the syndication API this pass. Two attached screenshots (presumed before/after context readout — not OCR'd at capture).

Quote-tweets [@tamarajtran](https://x.com/tamarajtran/status/2100694549362553153): *"found the perfect use case for @typesafeai Jev: instant compaction. in 2026, why is compaction still a summarization prompt? Jev can make it instant by scoring every tool call and dropping what's irrelevant."*

## Summary

The claim: run **Jev** (a small model from Typesafe AI) as a plugin inside Claude, where it reviews every tool call in the session context, scores each for relevance, and drops the irrelevant ones — as **compaction**. Volkov reports it took a session from **nearly 1M tokens to 86K** in **~1 second**, versus the standard summarization-prompt compaction (an LLM pass that costs time and tokens and loses fidelity).

The reframing from the quoted tweet: compaction in 2026 is still "ask a big model to summarize the transcript," when it could be a **filtering/scoring pass over discrete items** (tool calls) — cheap, instant, and selective rather than lossy-summarizing everything uniformly.

## Why it matters

- **Empirical follow-up to the Jev design-lens note.** [[2026-09-17-anthdm-jev-agent-memory]] flagged Jev as under-specified with no benchmark ("treat as a design lens, not an adoption recommendation"). This is the first measured data point: an installable plugin with a concrete 1M → 86K result and a 1s runtime. The two claims also converge: tamarajtran's "score every tool call, drop what's irrelevant" is exactly anthdm's *relevance* decision from the recall/store/merge/remove/relevance split — applied to compaction instead of memory.
- **Selective drop vs. uniform summarize is a real fork in context management.** Summarization compresses everything equally (lossy everywhere); relevance-scoring drops whole items losslessly where they matter. Same principle as mechanical pre-context filtering in [[2026-09-06-julian-risk-based-code-review]] — keep noise out of context by rule, not by asking the model to ignore it — and the same "harness-level primitive, not prompt logic" placement argued in [[2026-09-14-rauchg-verifiers-skills-new-frameworks]].
- **Directly relevant to our own stack.** We run long agent sessions (Hermes/Paperclip heartbeats, Claude Code) where context bloat and summarization-compaction fidelity loss are live costs. A 1s, ~92% context reduction with item-level selectivity would change session economics materially — worth a benchmark on our own transcripts.
- **Skepticism gates:** "1M → 86K in 1s" is self-reported by an enthusiastic newsletter author; screenshots not verified. The scorer deciding "irrelevant" can silently drop causally-needed state (a tool call whose output mattered three turns later) — summarization at least preserves a gist of everything. 150 replies suggest active debate; no independent benchmark yet. "Ask your Claude to install it" is viral phrasing, not documentation — check what the plugin actually does before trusting it with a session.
